newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea says may be ready for Korea peace talks.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea says may be ready for Korea peace talks.

text.p: North Korea said on Wednesday it would be ready to discuss peace on the Korean Peninsula with Washington and Seoul if they did not provoke a war.
"As long as the enemies do not provoke a war, we will press ahead with the peace process on the Korean Peninsula through dialogue and negotiations," Pyongyang's official newspaper Rodong Sinmun said.

"The Korean People's Army...is keeping a sharp eye on every move of the warmongers who are outwardly calling for 'four-way talks' to secure peace and security while waiting for a chance to trigger a war of aggression against the North," the North Korean daily said in an editorial in its Wednesday edition.
The report was carried by the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), which is monitored in Tokyo.

South Korean government sources said earlier on Wednesday that Pyongyang had agreed to a meeting of senior officials with South Korea, the United States and China to arrange four-way peace talks. The talks would be aimed at closing the books on the 1950-53 Korean War by replacing a fraying armistice with a permanent treaty between South Korea and the Stalinist North.

Seoul Foreign Ministry spokesman Lee Kyu-hyung declined to confirm the North Korean agreement but said: "There will be an announcement on four-way peace talks at 10 p.m. (1300 GMT) today." A similar announcement was due in Washington at the same time, Lee added.
